title: Old enough to drive?
description:
Get user input using input(“Enter your age: ”). If user is 18 or older, give feedback: You are old enough to drive. If below 18 give feedback to wait for the missing amount of years. Output:

```sh
Enter your age: 30
You are old enough to learn to drive.
Output:
Enter your age: 15
You need 3 more years to learn to drive.
```

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `check_driving_age(age)`, returning the exact feedback string, either `"You are old enough to learn to drive."` or `"You need {n} more years to learn to drive."` with `n` being the number of years left until 18.
examples:
check_driving_age(30) -> 'You are old enough to learn to drive.'
check_driving_age(15) -> 'You need 3 more years to learn to drive.'
hints: Compare age to 18 with a simple if / else.
When age is 18 or older, return the fixed 'old enough' message.
When age is below 18, compute the difference with 18 - age and insert it into an f-string.
expected_behavior: Returns a string telling the user whether they are old enough to drive (age >= 18), or how many more years they need to wait otherwise.

hidden_tests.expected: 'You are old enough to learn to drive.'
hidden_tests.label: well above 18

hidden_tests.expected: 'You need 3 more years to learn to drive.'
hidden_tests.label: below 18

hidden_tests.expected: 'You are old enough to learn to drive.'
hidden_tests.label: exactly 18 (boundary)

explanation: A single if / else checks whether age meets the 18-year threshold. When it does not, 18 - age gives exactly how many years remain, which is inserted into the feedback message with an f-string.
